why: I checked each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions against the words of its expect line. Checks 1, 3 and 4 stay within their lines. Check 1 compares the output to `HELLO, ADA!`. Check 3 needs the docs to describe or show usage of --shout. Check 4 needs the PR merged, HTTP 200 and `--shout` on the page. Check 2 goes further. Its PASS condition needs "the existing `greeting` and `cli` tests pass under npm test". Its FAIL condition triggers if "either existing test fails or has been changed". The expect line only says the CLI output without --shout is unchanged, and the first command (`test "$(node bin/greet.js Ada)" = "Hello, Ada!"`) already checks that. Requiring the `greeting()` unit test to pass, and failing a PR that edits the existing tests, are tests the words don't force. They should go under Advisory, not in the PASS or FAIL conditions.
